Important Conditions

  • Only one application per candidate against this CEN is permitted; multiple applications lead to rejection and debarment.
  • Vacancies are provisional and may increase, decrease, or become nil, per Railway Administration requirements.
  • A candidate with more than one qualifying discipline may choose only one Exam Group, and is then eligible only for posts mapped to that group.
  • Medical fitness as per the prescribed Medical Standard (A-3/B-1/B-2/C-1, as applicable to the post) is mandatory; no alternative appointment is given if found unfit.
  • Once a category/post/RRB is allotted, candidates forfeit the right to be considered for any other post/category in the same pay level.
  • Use of unfair means, impersonation, or false information leads to lifetime debarment from RRB/RRC exams and possible legal action.

How to Download the GSSSB Provisional Answer Key 2026

The general process GSSSB uses for candidate-specific provisional answer keys is as follows. Use this alongside the link shared in your own admit card or SMS/email notification.

  1. Open the official candidate response/answer key portal link provided in your GSSSB notice.
  2. Log in using your Advertisement Number, Confirmation Number, and Date of Birth, along with the captcha code.
  3. Navigate to the "Candidate Response" or "Provisional Answer Key" section.
  4. View your submitted responses alongside the provisional correct answers for each question.
  5. Use the print/download option to save your response sheet and answer key as a PDF for your records.

How to Raise an Objection

GSSSB generally accepts objections against a provisional answer key only through the online candidate portal, within the window mentioned in the specific notice. Objections sent by post, email, or in person are typically not entertained. As a general pattern (confirm against your own notice):

  • Log in to the candidate portal using your credentials.
  • Select the question(s) you wish to challenge, referencing the Question ID shown in your response sheet.
  • Upload supporting documentary proof (textbook references, official sources) for each objection.
  • Submit before the deadline stated in the notice late submissions are not accepted.
  • A subject-expert panel reviews all valid objections before GSSSB releases the Final Answer Key.

Required Documents

To access your personalized response sheet and raise objections, keep the following ready:

  • Advertisement number for the relevant post
  • Confirmation number / registration number from your application
  • Date of birth as per application records
  • Supporting reference material (books, official guidelines) if you plan to raise an objection

Important Instructions

  • This is a provisional answer key it can change after GSSSB reviews candidate objections, so do not treat it as final for score calculation.
  • Marks for any question later cancelled are usually awarded to all candidates on a pro-rata basis, as per GSSSB's standard practice in recent notices.
  • Objections are accepted online only, within the stated window; no other mode is entertained.
  • Keep a saved or printed copy of your response sheet for future reference, including for any grievance or RTI purposes.
  • The Final Answer Key, when released, supersedes this provisional key and forms the basis for the result.

The test was conducted for candidates from the outside-Karnataka and Kalyana-Karnataka quota applying to Village Administrative Officer (VAO), Land Surveyor, KREIS Teacher, Armed Police Constable (CAR/DAR/KSRP/IRB/KSISF), and Karnataka State Legal Services Authority (KSLSA) Section Officer posts who have not studied or passed their qualifying examination in Kannada.

The key answer has been published on the official KEA website, covering all four question paper versions A1, B1, C1, and D1. Candidates can now match their responses against the official key to estimate their probable score ahead of the final result. This article covers the download link, objection process, important dates, and answers to the questions candidates are asking most.

KEA Kannada Language Test 2026 What It Is

The Compulsory Kannada Language Test is a qualifying test, not a merit-ranking exam. It applies only to candidates from the outside-Karnataka and Kalyana-Karnataka quota who have not studied or passed their qualifying examination in Kannada, or who have not cleared an equivalent Kannada test, or who have not completed SSLC-level schooling with Kannada as a first or second language. Clearing this test alone does not guarantee final selection it is a mandatory clearance step for the candidates it applies to. The 22nd August 2026 sitting covered candidates applying for the following posts:

  • Police Department CAR/DAR/KSRP/IRB/KSISF Constable posts
  • Revenue Department Village Administrative Officer (VAO)
  • Land Surveyor posts (Department of Survey Settlement and Land Records)
  • Teacher posts under Karnataka Residential Education Institutions Society (KREIS)
  • Section Officer posts under the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority

How to Download KEA Kannada Language Test Answer Key 2026

  1. Visit the official KEA website at cetonline.karnataka.gov.in.

  3. Click on the relevant link for the answer key PDF.
  4. The answer key will display version-wise A1, B1, C1, and D1 on the screen.
  5. Match the answers against your version code and marked responses.
  6. Download and save the PDF for future reference and for use during objection filing.

KEA Kannada Language Test 2026 Objection Process

Candidates who wish to challenge any answer in the provisional key can do so through the official KEA Provisional Answer Key Objection Portal. The window is open from 22nd August 2026 until 24th August 2026, 12:00 noon, after which no objections will be accepted.

Steps to Raise an Objection

  1. Visit the objection portal login page at cetonline.karnataka.gov.in/keaobjections.
  2. Log in using your Application Number/Register Number and the first 5 characters of your name.
  3. Enter your Date of Birth.
  4. Select the examination Compulsory Kannada – 2026 (22-08-2026).
  5. Enter the captcha code and log in.
  6. Select the question number and version code you want to object to.
  7. Upload supporting documents or proof in PDF format for each objection.
  8. Pay the applicable fee of Rs. 25/- per objection and submit.

Important Instructions

  • Every objection must clearly mention the question number and version code, and must be supported by valid proof in PDF format.
  • A fee of Rs. 25/- is charged per objection raised; this fee is non-refundable.
  • Objections that do not correctly mention the question number or version code, or that lack valid supporting proof, will not be considered.
  • The decision of the subject expert committee reviewing the objections will be treated as final.
  • Objections cannot be submitted after 24th August 2026, 12:00 noon.

Also Read: HTET Result 2026

What Happens After the Objection Window Closes

Once the objection window closes on 24th August 2026, the subject expert committee will review all objections submitted by candidates. Based on this review, KEA will release the final answer key for the Kannada Language Test. Results will then be prepared using the final key, feeding into the overall selection process for the respective posts Police Constable, Village Administrative Officer, Land Surveyor, KREIS Teacher, and Section Officer. The exact date for the final key and result has not been officially announced yet.

RSSB Final Answer Key 2026: What It Means

A final answer key is the last, legally binding version of the answer key. RSSB releases it only after reviewing every objection candidates raised against the earlier provisional answer key. Once the final answer key is published, no further objections are accepted, and the board prepares the result strictly on the basis of this document.

  • For Lab Assistant 2026, the final answer key has been issued separately for Paper 01, Paper 02, and the Geography paper.
  • For Forester 2026, a single final answer key document has been released covering the Vanpal written exam.
  • Marks for any deleted or ambiguous questions, if applicable, are usually addressed in the final answer key or an accompanying notice check the official PDF for such remarks, since this detail was not independently confirmed at the time of writing.

About UPSC Indian Statistical Service (ISS) Examination 2026

The ISS Examination is one of the premier competitive exams conducted by UPSC to recruit officers for Group A and Group B posts in the Indian Statistical Service. Understanding the exam structure helps candidates correctly interpret the provisional answer key.

The Indian Statistical Service (ISS) Examination is conducted annually by the Union Public Service Commission to fill vacancies in the Indian Statistical Service, one of India's organised Group A Central Services. The exam tests candidates on subjects including Statistics, General English, and General Studies. The Statistics papers are the most technical and weightage-heavy components of the exam. The provisional answer key released covers the objective/multiple-choice components of the Statistics papers.

ISS Examination Paper Structure

The ISS Examination 2026 Statistics papers for which the provisional answer key has been released are:

  • Statistics Paper I - Covers topics such as Probability, Statistical Methods, Numerical Analysis, and related areas.
  • Statistics Paper II - Covers topics including Linear Models, Statistical Inference, Sampling Theory, and Econometrics.

How to Raise Objections Against UPSC ISS Provisional Answer Key 2026

If a candidate disagrees with any answer published in the provisional answer key, they can submit a formal representation to UPSC within the stipulated objection window period.

UPSC allows candidates to challenge answers in the provisional answer key by submitting a formal representation. The process for raising objections is as follows:

  • Download the provisional answer key PDF for the relevant paper.
  • Identify the question number(s) where you believe the answer is incorrect.
  • Prepare a written representation with supporting references from standard textbooks or study material.
  • Submit the representation to UPSC through the official channel specified in the answer key notification (typically by post or online submission to the UPSC office).
  • UPSC will review all representations received before publishing the Final Answer Key.

What Happens After the Provisional Answer Key?

After the provisional answer key is released and the objection window closes, UPSC reviews all valid representations before publishing the Final Answer Key.

Once the objection period ends, UPSC's subject matter experts review all representations submitted by candidates. Valid objections where an answer is found to be incorrect based on credible references result in changes to the final answer key. The Final Answer Key is then published on the official website. The final marks are computed based on the final (not provisional) answer key, which forms the basis for merit list preparation and eventual selection to the Indian Statistical Service.

Reviewed from recordings- did you ask, listen, and advise honestly? 5. Follow-up adherence. Every open lead contacted on schedule. 6. CRM hygiene. Logged same day, every day. 7. Conversions, site visits, and partner activations are tracked- but they're the company's scoreboard, not a quota over your head. Who fits: 1. Fluent Hindi and working English. 2. Comfortable dialling all day- reads a room over the phone. 3. Writes a clean CRM note. 4. Prior experience in real estate, interiors, edtech, or any high-volume inside sales floor is an advantage, not a requirement.

Job Description â Quantity Surveyor (QS Engineer)Position

Quantity Surveyor / QS Engineer â Civil Construction

Project: Commercial Hotel Construction Project

Location: Vijayawada / Amaravati, Andhra Pradesh

Site: Daspalla Project Site

Experience: 5+ Years

Employment Type: Full-time, Site-based

Job Summary

We are looking for an experienced Quantity Surveyor / QS Engineer with a minimum of 5 years of relevant experience in civil/building construction to join the project team for a commercial hotel construction project in Vijayawada/Amaravati.

The ideal candidate should have strong hands-on experience in quantity estimation, BOQ preparation, rate analysis, measurement, subcontractor billing, client billing, material reconciliation and cost control.

Candidates with experience in commercial buildings, hotels, high-rise buildings or large-scale building projects will be preferred.

Key Responsibilities

  • Prepare and review BOQs, quantity take-offs and estimates for civil and finishing works.
  • Prepare detailed quantity calculations from architectural, structural and MEP drawings.
  • Conduct regular site measurements and maintain accurate measurement records.
  • Prepare and verify contractor/subcontractor bills based on actual site measurements.
  • Review subcontractor RA bills, work orders, measurements and supporting documents.
  • Prepare client bills / RA bills and ensure timely submission.
  • Carry out rate analysis for various civil, structural and finishing items.
  • Monitor project quantities against the BOQ and identify variations.
  • Prepare and maintain variation statements, extra items and deviation statements.
  • Track project costs and assist in maintaining effective cost control.
  • Reconcile quantities of key materials such as cement, steel, concrete and other construction materials.
  • Coordinate with the Project Manager, Site Engineers, Planning Team, Purchase Team, Accounts Team and subcontractors.
  • Check drawings and specifications to identify quantity/cost implications before execution.
  • Maintain proper documentation of measurements, bills, work orders, quotations and quantity records.
  • Assist in preparing project cost forecasts and quantity/progress reports.
  • Support commercial negotiations with subcontractors and vendors when required.
  • Ensure that all billing and measurement documentation is accurate and submitted within project timelines.

Required Skills & Experience

  • 5+ years of experience as a Quantity Surveyor / QS Engineer in civil/building construction.
  • Diploma / B.E. / B.Tech in Civil Engineering or equivalent qualification.
  • Strong knowledge of BOQ preparation, quantity take-off, measurements and billing.
  • Good understanding of civil construction drawings and specifications.
  • Experience in subcontractor billing and client billing.
  • Strong knowledge of rate analysis and cost estimation.
  • Experience handling variation orders, extra items and reconciliation statements.
  • Good knowledge of Excel and quantity/billing-related software.
  • Ability to independently handle QS activities at a project site.
  • Strong analytical and numerical skills.
  • Good coordination and communication skills.

Preferred Candidate Profile

Candidates with experience in the following types of projects will be preferred:

  • Hotels / Hospitality Projects
  • Commercial Buildings
  • High-rise Buildings
  • Residential & Commercial Complexes
  • Large-scale Civil Construction Projects
